# Section 010: Extending The Kubernetes API With CRDs

The reader designs a platform service as a new Kubernetes resource type. First the schema that makes the API server type, default, prune and reject input, then versions and subresources so the API can evolve and a controller can report status. It comes first because every later section (operators, Crossplane, self-service) is built on custom resources and reads their schema and status.

**Curriculum item covered:** Designing and Creating Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) for Platform Services

---

## What You Will Master

- Write a CustomResourceDefinition in apiextensions.k8s.io/v1 with a structural openAPIV3Schema for a platform service
- Mark fields as required and constrain them with enum, minimum, maximum and pattern
- Set default values and predict which unknown fields the API server prunes
- Write a CEL rule in x-kubernetes-validations, including a transition rule that uses oldSelf
- Add additionalPrinterColumns and a shortName so kubectl get shows the important fields
- Prove a rule works by applying a custom resource the API server must reject
- Add a second version to a CRD and choose which version is served and which is the storage version
- Read which version an object is stored in from status.storedVersions
- Mark a version deprecated and read the warning kubectl prints
- Enable the status subresource and show that a spec update cannot change status
- Enable the scale subresource and scale a custom resource with kubectl scale

## The Learning Path

### 1. Design A CRD Schema That Validates Input
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Design A CRD Schema That Validates Input](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-010/module-01/playground` — kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.35) with no add-ons. A starter CRD `teamenvironments.platform.starfleet.io` (kind TeamEnvironment) is applied with a deliberately weak schema (x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields on spec, no required fields, no printer columns), plus three example manifests on disk: a valid TeamEnvironment, one with a typo in a field name, and one with an out-of-range replica count, all of which the weak schema accepts. Namespaces `starfleet` and `outpost` exist. No controller acts on the CRD, so status stays empty on purpose.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS019.git -c sections/section-010/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Version A CRD And Enable Subresources
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Version A CRD And Enable Subresources](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-010/module-02/playground` — kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.35) with no add-ons. The TeamEnvironment CRD is installed with a full schema in one version only (v1alpha1), with two TeamEnvironment objects already stored in v1alpha1 in namespace `outpost`. No status or scale subresource is enabled yet. A v1 schema file that renames nothing (so None conversion is safe) is provided for the reader to add. No controller runs; the reader acts as the controller with kubectl patch --subresource=status.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS019.git -c sections/section-010/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Publish A Validated And Versioned Platform API Capstone — `sections/section-010/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS019.git -c sections/section-010/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** The platform team must publish a `Database` API for tenant teams. The reader writes the CRD with required and defaulted fields, a CEL rule that forbids shrinking storage, printer columns, a second served version with v1 as the storage version, and status and scale subresources, then proves invalid requests are rejected and existing objects are still readable.
